is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles coluzzii and Anopheles melas on Bioko Island (page 4).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports genotyping for Vgsc L995F (kdr 1014F), L995S (kdr 1014S), N1575Y, and Ace-1 G119S (Table 1, page 3).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 1 on page 3 provides the number of specimens and the frequency of genotypes (1014F/F, 1014F/L, 1014L/L) for populations collected in 2011 and 2015.

african_field_population.evidence: The study uses field-caught mosquitoes from Bioko Island, Equatorial Guinea (page 4).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an empirical study reporting new field collections and laboratory functional characterization of CYP9K1.

sub_country_location.evidence: The study specifies collection sites in Malabo, Bioko Island, with coordinates provided for the hospital and industrial sites (page 4).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The study reports specific collection years (2011, 2014, 2015) for the intensive surveys (page 4).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The paper mentions using data from a previous study (Hemingway et al., 2013) for 2011 comparisons, but the 2015 data is new primary data.

supplement.evidence: All necessary genotype data is provided in Table 1 of the main text.

assessment.summary: This study investigates the rapid evolution of pyrethroid resistance in Anopheles coluzzii on Bioko Island, Equatorial Guinea, following the reintroduction of pyrethroid-based IRS. It documents a significant increase in the frequency of the L1014F kdr mutation and identifies the overexpression of the cytochrome P450 gene CYP9K1 as a key metabolic resistance mechanism, which was functionally validated to metabolize deltamethrin.
